candidates.title: Binder-family calibration of 7-day strength for 28-day qualification

candidates.new_claim: It proposes that a common 7-day proxy may be miscalibrated across binder families; this is a conjecture, not an established result.
candidates.domain_value: Could show whether a 7-day test can support early mix qualification or whether the team should use a binder-family-specific threshold or wait for later testing. This affects testing schedule and qualification decisions, not just prediction error.
assumptions: Rows at the same seven ingredient quantities and different ages can be treated as formulation-level age contrasts, while still not being assumed to be the same batch or curing environment.
A day-7/day-28 strength ratio is interpretable only for positive strengths and is a descriptive proxy, not a causal hydration measure.
SCM share is defined as (Blast Furnace Slag + Fly Ash)/(Cement + Blast Furnace Slag + Fly Ash); binder mass is positive in the supplied domain.

candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Potentially, using the supplied full table if exact formulation repeats at ages 7 and 28 exist in both groups; feasibility is unknown until checked. No batch-level causal inference is feasible from the documented fields.
